title: Real-time Telemetry Representative Sampling
business: IoT sensor network operators managing high-velocity data streams.
problem: Storing every data point from millions of sensors is cost-prohibitive, yet simple truncation loses long-term trends and introduces bias toward early data.
solution: Reservoir Sampling maintains a fixed-size representative sample of a stream of unknown length, ensuring every element has an equal probability of being selected without needing to know the total stream size in advance.
steps: Initialize a reservoir array of fixed size k.
Fill the reservoir with the first k elements from the incoming stream.
For each subsequent element at index i (where i > k), generate a random integer j between 0 and i.
If j is less than k, replace the element at index j in the reservoir with the new element from the stream.
outcome: A statistically unbiased subset of the total stream that allows for accurate trend analysis without the storage overhead of the full dataset.
limitation: The primary limitation is that it assumes a uniform distribution of importance across the stream; it cannot prioritize recent data or specific event types without modifying the probability logic, which can be checked by verifying if the sample distribution matches the historical stream distribution over time.

questions.question: In Real-time Telemetry Representative Sampling, why is this technique used instead of simple truncation?
options: To ensure every element has an equal probability of being selected without knowing the total stream size.
To prioritize the most recent data points over historical data.
To reduce the computational complexity of sorting the stream.
To increase the storage capacity of the IoT sensor network.
questions.explanation: Reservoir Sampling is specifically designed to handle unknown stream lengths while maintaining statistical representation, which simple truncation fails to do.
questions.evidence: Reservoir Sampling maintains a fixed-size representative sample of a stream of unknown length, ensuring every element has an equal probability of being selected without needing to know the total stream size in advance.

questions.question: What is a key limitation of the Real-time Telemetry Representative Sampling approach?
options: It requires the total stream size to be known before processing starts.
It cannot handle high-velocity data streams efficiently.
It assumes a uniform distribution of importance and cannot prioritize specific data types without logic changes.
It consumes more memory than storing the full dataset.
questions.explanation: The technique is inherently uniform, meaning it treats all data points equally, which is a limitation if the business needs to prioritize specific events.
